body: This will happily convert strings like `+++5` to 5. Is this wanted behavior?

These functions are unnecessarily inefficient, but they're designed after the current `to_int` function, so it's fine. Tools to make them efficient are not fully in place yet so I'll think this is appropriate for now.
thought it kept the code cleaner and it seemed like a benign edge case.
with clamp it would eval to 0 without it would error as unsupported. Again thought about keeping the parser simple with less conditionals to check.
This was again intentional of parse the number and then drop anything that isn't the number after it like a decimal, space, new line or any other junk.

Yes, that was the correct decision :) Feel free to close this one.
I think it's good to be correct even in "benign" edge cases because sooner or later, somebody will run into these and then the function has to be changed.
The other code explicitly supports -----5, so it would be weird to not support +++++5.
